channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: Baghdad centralizes Kurdish oil fields; Erbil rejects move as 'unacceptable'
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iraqi PM Zeydi linked northern oil fields to federal control after smuggling investigation; KRG's Barzani called the move "entirely unacceptable." (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Saudi jets strike Hodeidah; Sanaa names all Saudi Red Sea ports as targets
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Saudi warplanes hit Yemen's Hodeidah port and international airport; Houthi spokesman warned all Saudi ports on the Red Sea are now targets. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Iran's press says 'CIA cyberattack'; U.S. says classified systems unaffected
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: CIA and ODNI's open-source intelligence network was breached; U.S. officials said classified systems were not compromised. (Source: Donya-e Eqtesad)

item.title: Truckers in Iran strike for third day; cargo halted in 15 cities
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Protesting dollar-based price hikes on tires and fuel, truckers across 15 Iranian cities stopped hauling cargo for the third consecutive day. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: In Ekbatan case, execution halted at last minute; UN calls for M.A. and N.N.
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Executions of M.A. and N.N. in Ekbatan case halted last minute after families and UN pressure; case enters third year. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Turkey-Iran relations: trade, natural gas, borders, and regional rivalry
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Turkey and Iran share a 1639 border, pursue $30B annual trade, have a 1996 gas deal ending in 2026, and face migration and smuggling pressure. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Three tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, burst into flames; stern warning from IRGC Navy
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: IRGC Navy announced three tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in Strait of Hormuz; U.S. air support failed to prevent the incident. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Central Bank chief: Our reserves eroded by $51 billion since Iran war began
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Central Bank chief Karahan announced gross reserves fell from $210 billion to $159 billion since war began—a $51 billion decline. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: U.S. Treasury sanctions Iran shadow banking: 8 individuals, 22 companies targeted
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Treasury designates 8 Iranians and 22 companies under Operation Economic Outcast; FinCEN identifies $14.7 billion in suspicious transactions. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Kalibaf: The enemy wants to impose a grinding 'neither war nor peace' on Iran
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Parliament Speaker Kalibaf said the enemy seeks to impose grinding 'neither war nor peace' on Iran; permanent deterrence is the way out. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Three Bahai citizens detained in Kerman; one in Semnan called in for interrogation twice
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Intelligence Ministry officials detained three Bahai citizens in Kerman; a Bahai in Semnan was called in for questioning on consecutive days. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Reading Iran's economy: rial-toman, official/free-market rates, inflation, and oil exports
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: The rial-toman distinction, official and parallel exchange rates, chronic inflation, and sanctioned oil exports; a guide to reading Iran's economy. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Trump to Fox News: If no deal, we can strike Iran after the new year
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Trump told Fox News that without an Iran deal, strikes are possible after the new year, and would sink ships breaking the blockade. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Jeffries and Carlson met at the same point: The Iran war must end
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Democratic leader Jeffries and conservative Carlson, for different reasons, blamed the U.S. Iran war for economic and political crisis. (Source: Ettelaat)

item.title: Fidan: Turkey supports Saudi Arabia's security, but won't send troops
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Foreign Minister Fidan said Turkey backs Saudi Arabia's security but troop deployment requires parliamentary approval. (Source: Kayhan (from Persian))

item.title: Session canceled in Iranian parliament: tablet malfunction or brawl?
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iranian parliament's Sunday session was canceled; Kayhan blamed tablet malfunction, one deputy blamed rocking and physical fighting. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Methanol poisoning in Shiraz and Marvdasht: 30 hospitalized, 1 dead
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: In 24 hours, 30 people in Shiraz and Marvdasht were hospitalized with methanol poisoning, 1 died; death toll in Nishapur rose to 4. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Weekly Framework (November 16-22): Blockade breached at Hormuz, regional fire reignited in the Gulf
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Persian press this week: oil flow halved at Hormuz, renewed fire exchanges in Bahrain-Riyadh-Jeddah, Abadan protests and winter hardship. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: Iran's nuclear program: what are the NPT, the JCPOA, and the 'trigger mechanism'?
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: NPT, IAEA oversight, JCPOA limits, enrichment rates, and the snapback mechanism explained chronologically from 1970 to 2026. (Source: Farsçadan)

item.title: IRGC claims Patriot radar strike on Bahrain bases; Bahrain and U.S. do not confirm
item.dc:creator: Farsçadan Editors
item.description: Iran's IRGC announced striking two Patriot radars at U.S. bases in Bahrain; Bahrain called UN Security Council meeting. (Source: Khabaronline)
